αἶψ: αἶψα — quickly, swiftly; adv., elided (αἶψ’ = αἶψα)
αὐδήεσσα: αὐδήεις — endowed with speech or voice (from αὐδή); anciently explained as ’speaking with a human voice’, exact force debated; fem. nom. sg.
αὐτίκ: αὐτίκα (elided αὐτίκ’) — at once, immediately, forthwith; adv.
αὐτούς: αὐτός — self; masc. acc. pl.: ’them’ · also intensive, ’the very men themselves’ (with a following τε … τε) · also ’ourselves’, first person, coordinate with another object (νῆάς τε καὶ αὐτούς ’both the ships and ourselves’)
αὐτοὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’themselves’ · also intensive in agreement with an unexpressed ’we’: ’we ourselves’ (αὐτοὶ βῆμεν ’we ourselves stepped out’) · also in agreement with an unexpressed ’you’: ’you yourselves’ (αὐτοὶ δ’ ὀτρύνεσθε ’and you yourselves rouse yourselves’)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο) · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun: σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ ’and of yourself’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun of a thing, ’from it’, after ἐκ (ἐκ δ’ αὐτοῦ πείρατ’ ἀνήφθω, of the mast)
αὐτόθι: αὐτόθι — here, on the spot, right there; adv.
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg.: ’himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼν αὐτός) · also masc. nom. sg. with a 2nd-person subject: ’yourself’ (εἰδήσεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός ’you will see for yourself’)
αὐτῆς: αὐτός — self; fem. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (τὰ σ’ αὐτῆς ἔργα ’your own works’): ’of yourself’ · also plain gen. sg. governed by ἄγχι ’near, close to’: ’her’ (ἄγχι δ’ αὐτῆς ’close beside her’) · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of a ship, fem.), governed by a noun: χρεὼ ... αὐτῆς ’a need of it’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’it’ (of a raft, fem.), governed by a preposition: ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ’upon it’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun ’her’, possessive with a noun: νόος ... αὐτῆς ’her mind’
αὐτῶν: αὐτός — self; gen. pl.: ’their own’ (reinforcing a possessive) · also plain neut. gen. pl. personal pronoun, not reinforcing a possessive: ’them’ (λήσομαι αὐτῶν ’I will forget them’, of things said) · also intensive with a noun: ’of the heroes themselves’ (αὐτῶν ἡρώων) · also with the article, ’the same’: τοκήων τῶν αὐτῶν ’the very same parents’ · also masc./neut. gen. pl. personal pronoun, ’their’ (αὐτῶν τε φθογγήν ’their voice’, of the creatures on the far shore) · also gen. pl. ’our own’, possessive of the speaker’s group, with no other possessive (αὐτῶν … ἀφραδίῃσιν ’through our own follies’) · also masc. gen. pl., partitive: ’of them’ (οὐδέ τις αὐτῶν ’not one of them’) · also masc. gen. pl. personal pronoun after a preposition: ’them’ (δι’ αὐτῶν ’through the midst of them’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
βοήσας: βοάω — shout, cry out; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having shouted’
βοῦς: βοῦς — ox, cow; pl. ’cattle’; acc. pl. · also masc./fem. nom. sg. (same spelling as the acc. pl.): ’the ox, the heifer’ (ἦλθε ... βοῦς ’the heifer came’)
βοῶν: βοῦς — ox, cow; pl. ’cattle’; gen. pl.
βροτοῖσιν: βροτός — mortal, mortal man; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οῖς)
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γέγωνε: γέγωνα (defective, akin to γεγωνέω) — be audible, make oneself heard; perf. 3 sg. with pres. force
γένηται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’shall come’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a direct question of doubt/deliberation, no ἄν/κε: τί … γένηται; ’what is to happen?’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg., prospective in a negative statement with a relative clause: οὐδὲ γένηται ’nor ever shall there be’
γίγνεται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen, arise; pres. 3 sg. (χρεὼ γίγνεται ’a need arises’) · also copular, ’is, comes to be’ (φωνὴ … γίγνεται ’the voice is’)
γαλήνη: γαλήνη — calm (of the sea); fem. nom. sg.
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γλαφυρῇ: γλαφυρός — hollow, hollowed out; fem. dat. sg.
γόνος: γόνος — offspring, child; masc. nom. sg.
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δαίμων: δαίμων — a god, some divine power (vague, unspecified); masc. nom. sg.
δείδω: δείδω (= δέδοικα) — fear, be afraid; pres. 1 sg., + μή and a verb: ’I fear that…’
δεινόν: δεινός — terrible, dread, awesome; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
δεινὴ: δεινός — dread, terrible, awesome; fem. nom. sg.
δεσμοῖσι: δεσμός — bond, fetter; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οῖς)
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
διατμήξας: διατμήγω — cut apart, split; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ‘having split apart’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’ · also with opt., in a wish: ’if only’ (εἰ … ὁμοφρονέοις … γένοιο) · also ὡς εἰ + opt., ’as if’ (ὡς εἰ … ἱκοίατο ’as if they had come’)
εἰδότες: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. pl.: ‘knowing’
εἰδώς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’) · also in the idiom εἰς ὅ (κε) ’until’: εἰς ὅ κεν … μιγήῃς ’until you mingle with’
εἰσίν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 pl.: ’they are’ (Attic form, alongside the epic by-form ἔασιν)
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’) · also with opt., of an aim in view: ’in case, to see if’ (εἴ τινά … λάβοι ’in case he might catch someone’) · also in ὡς εἴ τ’ + opt., ’as if’
εἴσβαινον: εἰσβαίνω — go aboard, embark; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= εἰσέβαινον)
εὐρείῃ: εὐρύς — broad, wide; fem. dat. sg., epic -είῃ (= Attic -είᾳ)
θέσαν: τίθημι — put, make; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἔθεσαν): ’made’ (ἀνάπυστα θέσαν ’made known’)
θέσφαθ: θέσφατος — decreed by a god; neut. pl. noun, ’oracles’, elided (θέσφαθ’ = θέσφατα)
θεά: θεά — goddess; nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form): ’goddess!’
θεάων: θεά — goddess; gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic θεῶν)
θεοῖσιν: θεός — god; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οις)
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’) · also of a goddess (θεός is common gender) · also nom. sg. subject, of a god already introduced by epithets but not yet named: ’the god’
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κίρκη: Κίρκη — Circe, the enchantress goddess; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg., address: ’Circe!’ (ὦ Κίρκη)
καθῖζον: καθίζω — sit down, take one’s seat; impf. 3 pl.
κακά: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl., substantive: ’evils, troubles’ (πάθομεν κακά ’we suffered troubles’)
κακόν: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. sg.: ’a bad thing, evil’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal passive (κακόν τ’ ἀγαθόν τε τέτυκται ’whatever, good or bad, has come to pass’) · also neut. nom. sg. adjective agreeing with πέλωρ: ’evil’ (πέλωρ κακόν ’an evil monster’)
κακῶς: κακός — bad, evil; adv.: ’wickedly, shamefully’ · also ’miserably, in misery’ (ὀψὲ κακῶς ἔλθοι ’may he come late, in misery’)
καλά: καλός — good, fine, beautiful; neut. nom./acc. pl.
καρπαλίμως: καρπάλιμος — swift, nimble; adv. καρπαλίμως: ’swiftly, nimbly’
κατόπισθε: κατόπισθε(ν) — behind, after; adv., or prep. + gen.: ’behind’
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (κατὰ πετράων ’down from the rocks’) · also + gen., ’all over, throughout’ (κατὰ σπείους κέχυτο ’lay spread all over the cave’) · also + acc., of the part grasped: ’by’ (κατὰ νῶτα λαβών ’taking him by the back’) · also + acc., ’on account of, on the business of’ (κατὰ χρέος ’on business’) · also + gen., ’down in, within’ (κατὰ σπείους κοίλοιο δέδυκεν ’is sunk in the hollow cave’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’)
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’ · also + subj. in a relative clause, prospective: ’who is to, who will’ (ἥ κεν ἄγῃσι ’(a wagon) that shall carry’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … δαινύῃ ’whenever you feast’) · also + subj. in the protasis of a condition after αἴ: ’if ever’ · also + opt., potential: ’might, may’
κεῖθι: κεῖθι — there; adv., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖ)
κιὼν: κίω — go; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’going’
κληῖσι: κληΐς — thole-pin, oarlock (also ’key, bolt’ elsewhere); fem. dat. pl., epic -ισι · also ’rowing-bench, thwart’ (ἐπὶ κληῖσι καθῖζον ’sat down on the rowing-benches’)
κοίμησε: κοιμάω — put to bed, lull to sleep; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἐκοίμησε)
κυανοπρῴροιο: κυανόπρῳρος — dark-prowed; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with νεός
κυβερνήτης: κυβερνήτης — helmsman, steersman; masc. nom. sg.
κῆρ: κῆρ — heart; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect (φίλον κῆρ ’in his own heart’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a verb: κῆρ ἤθελε ’my heart wished’
κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
κῦδος: κῦδος — glory, the lustre of success granted by a god; neut. nom./acc. sg.
λάθεν: λανθάνω — escape the notice of (+ acc.); aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔλαθεν)
λῦσαί: λύω — loose, release, let go; aor. inf. act., used as an imperative: ’release!, let go!’ · also complementary inf. after κελεύω: ’to release’ (ἑτάρους λῦσαί τε κελεύῃς ’bid your companions release you’)
λῦσαι: λύω — loose, untie; aor. inf.: ’to loose (the stern-cables)’
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big, tall; masc. acc. sg.
μέγας: μέγας — great, big, grown; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’grown’ · also plain attributive adj., masc. nom. sg., ’great, huge’ (μέγας σῦς ’a great boar’), not predicate
μέδηαι: μέδομαι — be mindful of, think of (+ gen.); pres. subj. 2 sg. mid., epic -ηαι (= Attic μέδῃ)
μέλαν: μέλας — black, dark; neut. nom./acc. sg.
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’ · also negating a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’so that … not’ (ἵνα μή τι … ἀλγήσετε ’so that you may not suffer’)
μεγάλη: μέγας — great, large; fem. nom. sg.
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μυθήσατο: μυθέομαι — speak, say, tell; aor. 3 sg.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’
μῆλα: μῆλον — sheep, goat, flock-animal; neut. nom. pl.: ’the flocks’ · also neut. acc. pl. (same form), direct object: ἦγον ... μῆλα ’they led sheep’
ναίειν: ναίω — dwell, inhabit; pres. inf.: ’to dwell’ (in a wish with ὄφελον)
νεὸς: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. sg., epic-Ionic (= Attic νεώς)
νεῖαι: νέομαι — go, come back; pres. 2 sg., contracted epic νεῖαι (= νέεαι), future sense: ’you will come back’
νηί: ναῦς (epic νηῦς) — ship; fem. dat. sg. νηί
νημερτὲς: νημερτής — unerring, infallible; neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’the unerring truth’
νηνεμίη: νηνεμίη — windlessness, calm without wind; fem. nom. sg.
νηῦς: ναῦς — ship; nom. sg., epic νηῦς
νύμφαι: νύμφη — nymph; also bride; fem. nom. pl.
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
οἰῶν: ὄϊς (Attic οἶς) — sheep; masc./fem. gen. pl., contracted (= epic ὀίων)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’)
οἴους: οἶος — alone, only; masc. acc. pl.: ’only, alone’ (δύ’ οἴους ’two only’)
οἶον: οἶος — alone, only; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., agreeing with the subject: ’standing alone’ (ὅ τε φαίνεται οἶον ’which appears alone’)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὖρον: οὖρος — fair wind, following wind; masc. acc. sg. · also a different word, neut. ’furrow-stretch’, the length a pair of mules ploughs in one go (οὖρον … ἡμιόνοιιν); exact measure unknown
οὖρος: οὖρος — a fair wind, favorable wind; masc. nom. sg. · also a different word, related to ὁράω ’see, watch’ — warden, guardian; masc. nom. sg. (οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν ’warden of the Achaeans’)
πάνθ: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom. pl., elided and aspirated (πάνθ’ = πάντα): ’everything’
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάσχοντες: πάσχω — suffer, experience; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
πέρ: περ — even, indeed; intensive/concessive particle, accented πέρ before the enclitic τε/τις that follows it; with εἰ: ’even if’
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
παρὲξ: παρέξ — beside, past, beyond; adv./prep. + acc., here adverbial with εἴποιμι: ’say otherwise, speak beside the point’ · also adv. with ἐλάσωσιν, ’past, beyond’ (τάς γε παρὲξ ἐλάσωσιν ’drive past them’)
πατρώια: πατρώιος — of one’s father, ancestral; neut. acc. pl.
πείρατ: πεῖραρ — end, limit; of a rope, its ends; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (πείρατ’ = πείρατα)
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
πιέζειν: πιέζω — press, squeeze hard, grip; pres. inf. act., used as an imperative: ’press hard, grip!’
πλεόνεσσι: πολύς — much, many; comparative πλέων/πλείων, masc. dat. pl. πλεόνεσσι, epic -εσσι (= Attic πλείοσι)
πλησίον: πλησίος — near, neighbouring; neut. acc. sg. as adv. πλησίον: ’near, beside’
πλησίστιον: πλησίστιος — filling the sail; adj., masc. acc. sg., with οὖρον
πολιὴν: πολιός — grey, hoary; adj., fem. acc. sg. (πολιὴν ἅλα ’the grey sea’)
πολλαὶ: πολύς — much, many; fem. nom. pl.
πολὺ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’by far’ · also neut. nom. sg. adj. agreeing with ὕδωρ: ’much, plentiful’
πονησάμενοι: πονέομαι — labour at, busy oneself with; aor. part. mid. masc. nom. pl., + acc.: ’having seen to’
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
πουλυβοτείρῃ: πολυβότειρα — much-nourishing, giving much pasture; fem. dat. sg., epic πουλυ- (= Attic πολυβοτείρᾳ), epithet of the earth
πρίν: πρίν — before, until; conj./adv., + inf. (like Attic πρίν) · also + a temporal clause (πρίν γ’ ὅτ’ ἄν + subj.): ’until the time when’ · also πρίν κε + opt., an independent potential clause answering a suppressed protasis: ’sooner, before then’ (πρίν κεν ... ἵκοιο ’you would arrive home before then’) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article, no inf.: ’formerly, at first’ (parallel to the by-form πρὶν)
προσέειπον: προσεῖπον (aor. of πρόσφημι) — speak to, address; aor. 1 sg.
πρυμνήσια: πρυμνήσιον — stern-cable (mooring rope); neut. acc. pl.
πρῶτον: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first’
πως: πώς — somehow, in any way; enclitic adv. (οὔ πως ’in no way’)
πόδας: πούς — foot; acc. pl., accusative of respect
πόνος: πόνος — toil, labour, hardship; masc. nom. sg.
πότνια: πότνια — lady, mistress (title of respect for a goddess); fem. nom. sg. · also of a mortal woman, a respectful title: ’revered, honoured’ (πότνια μήτηρ ’the honoured mother’)
πώ: πώ — yet, up to now; enclitic adv. (usually with a negative)
πώεα: πῶυ — flock (of sheep); neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
πῆμα: πῆμα — woe, calamity, disaster; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., direct object: ’woe’
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’
σίνηαι: σίνομαι — harm, damage, plunder; pres. subj. 2 sg. mid., epic -ηαι (= Attic σίνῃ)
σειρήνοιιν: Σειρήν — Siren; fem. gen. dual, ’of the two Sirens’
σκοπέλῳ: σκόπελος — rock, crag, cliff; masc. dat. sg.
σκόπελον: σκόπελος — rock, crag, cliff; masc. acc. sg.
στιβαρῇσι: στιβαρός — stout, sturdy, strong; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -αῖς)
σχέτλιε: σχέτλιος — reckless, cruel; masc. voc. sg.: ’you reckless one!’
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’
τέκε: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔτεκε)
τέκεν: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, movable ν (= ἔτεκεν)
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεκμαίρομ: τεκμαίρομαι — fix, mark out, ordain; pres. 1 sg. mid., elided (τεκμαίρομ’ = τεκμαίρομαι)
τηλόθι: τηλόθι — far off, far away; epic adv. with suffix -θι, + gen.: ’far from’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῦτο: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τρὶς: τρίς — three times, thrice; numeral adv.
τόσα: τόσος — so much, so many; correlative demonstrative adj., neut. acc. pl.: ’so much’
τόσσον: τόσος (epic τόσσος) — so much, so great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’so much’
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τόφρα: τόφρα — so long, meanwhile; adv., correlative with ἕως ’until’
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’)
τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ‘them, those’ (referring to ships) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the mules · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cattle · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the fruits
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg. · also fem. gen. sg. with the force of a relative: ’of which’ (τῆς ἕτερον μὲν θειλόπεδον ’of which one part is a drying-ground’)
τῇδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this (here); demonstrative pron., fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ’here, in this place’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’)
φίλοι: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. nom. pl.: ’dear (guest-friends)’ · also masc. voc. pl. (identical form), direct address: ’friends!’ (δεῦτε, φίλοι) · also attributive, with a noun: φίλοι υἷες ’dear sons’
φθινύθουσι: φθινύθω — waste away, wither; pres. 3 pl.
φθόγγον: φθόγγος — voice, sound; masc. acc. sg.
φυγέειν: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic φυγεῖν)
φυλασσέμεναι: φυλάσσω — guard, watch over; pres. inf., epic -έμεναι (= Attic φυλάσσειν)
φύγοιμεν: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. opt. 1 pl., in a purpose clause: ’that we might escape’
φύλλοισι: φύλλον — leaf; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι
φῶτας: φώς — man, warrior, mortal; masc. acc. pl.
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χθονὶ: χθών — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
χρυσόθρονος: χρυσόθρονος — golden-throned; adj., fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses (an old alternative derives the second element from θρόνα ’embroidered flowers’)
χρὴ: χρή — it is necessary, it is right; impersonal verb + acc. and inf. · also + acc. of the person and gen. of the thing: ’there is need of’
ἀθάνατον: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc./fem. acc. sg.
ἀθανάτοισιν: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀκουέμεν: ἀκούω — hear, listen to; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἀκούειν)
ἀλλήλων: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., gen. pl.
ἀλύξῃς: ἀλύσκω — escape, avoid; aor. subj. 2 sg.: ’you escape’
ἀμβαίνειν: ἀναβαίνω — go up, go aboard; pres. inf., epic ἀμβαίνειν (ἀνα- apocopated to ἀμ- before β), as an instruction
ἀμείβετο: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented
ἀμειβόμενος: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. masc. nom. sg. mid.
ἀμυναίμην: ἀμύνω — ward off, defend; aor. opt. 1 sg. mid.: ’I would defend myself’
ἀνά: ἀνά — up, up along; prep. + acc., or adv. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’mounted’); acute kept before an enclitic
ἀνήφθω: ἀνάπτω — fasten to, tie up; perf. imper. pass. 3 sg.: ’let it be fastened’
ἀνίησιν: ἀνίημι — send up, let go, release; pres. 3 sg.
ἀνστάντες: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; intrans. aor. part. masc. nom. pl., epic apocope (ἀνστάντες = ἀναστάντες)
ἀνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., + inf.: ’was bidding’ · also pres. 3 sg., a present formed on the perf. stem: ’bids’ (ἐποτρύνει καὶ ἀνώγει ’urges and bids’)
ἀνὰ: ἀνά — up along, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνὰ … κέρασσεν, from ἀνακεράννυμι ’mix up’) · also + gen., ’up onto’ (ἀνὰ νηὸς ἔβην ’I went up on board’) · also + acc., proportional, ’to, at the rate of’ (ἀνὰ εἴκοσι μέτρα ’at twenty measures (of water) to the one cup’) · also in tmesis with a verb of signalling, construed with a dat.: ἀνὰ … ὀφρύσι νεῦον ’I signalled with raised brows’ · also + acc. θυμόν, ’in (their) heart’ (ἀνὰ θυμὸν ἐθάμβεον ’they were amazed in their hearts’) · also + dat., ’on, upon’ (ἀνὰ φαιδίμῳ ὤμῳ ’on the shining shoulder’)
ἀπ: ἀπό (elided ἀπ’) — from, away from; prep. + gen.
ἀπήμων: ἀπήμων — unharmed, safe; adj., masc./fem. nom. sg. (νόστος ἀπήμων ’a safe homecoming’)
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀπῆμεν: ἄπειμι — be away, be distant; impf. 1 pl., epic (= Attic ἀπῇμεν): ’we were away’
ἀργαλέον: ἀργαλέος — hard, difficult, troublesome; neut. nom. sg., impersonal predicate governing an inf. · also neut. acc. sg. agreeing with a noun: ’grievous, hard’ (δεινόν τ’ ἀργαλέον τε, of λαῖτμα) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative in a double acc.: ’hard’ (τὸν … ἀργαλέον θήσει ’will make it hard’)
ἀργεῖοι: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀσινέας: ἀσινής — unharmed, unscathed; fem. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀσινεῖς)
ἀφίξεαι: ἀφικνέομαι — come to, arrive at; fut. 2 sg. mid., epic -εαι (= Attic ἀφίξῃ)
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀχνύμενος: ἄχνυμαι — grieve, be vexed, be distressed; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. acc. pl.
ἄγ: ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (ἄγ’ = ἄγε): ’he led’ · also ἄγε (elided ἄγ’), the interjection ’come!’, 2 sg. imper., used even to a group: ’come, come now’
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄγριον: ἄγριος — wild, savage; masc. acc. sg.
ἄνακτος: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. gen. sg.
ἄπο: ἀπό — away from, from; + gen.; accented ἄπο when it follows its noun (anastrophe: φίλων ἄπο) · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ὀλέσαντ’ ἄπο = ἀπολέσαντα ’having lost’)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἅ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’what things’
ἅλα: ἅλς — sea, salt sea; fem. acc. sg.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐάᾳς: ἐάω — allow, leave alone; pres. subj. 2 sg., epic ἐάᾳς (= Attic ἐᾷς)
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows) · also accented ἐγώ before the enclitic μιν that follows
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλάαν: ἐλαύνω — drive; epic pres. inf. of the by-form ἐλάω, with diectasis (contracted ἐλᾶν; Attic pres. inf. ἐλαύνειν): ’to drive on’ · also, same spelling, fut. inf. (Attic ἐλᾶν): ’to be going to drive’, told apart only by context
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνίσπες: ἐνέπω/ἐνίσπω — tell, relate, declare; aor. imper. 2 sg.: ’tell!’
ἐνοσίχθων: ἐνοσίχθων — earth-shaker, epithet of Poseidon (from ἔνοσις ’shaking’ + χθών ’earth’); nom. sg.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξαῦτις: ἐξαῦτις — again, once more, anew; adv., epic (= Attic αὖθις)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπαύσατο: παύω (mid.) — cease, stop; aor. mid. 3 sg., intransitive
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐρετμοῖς: ἐρετμόν — oar; neut. dat. pl., instrumental: ’with oars’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλὸν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; neut./masc. acc. sg.
ἐυπλόκαμος: ἐϋπλόκαμος — fair-tressed, with fine hair; fem. nom. sg. (Calypso’s standing epithet) · also used of Demeter (5.125), so not unique to Calypso despite the parenthetical above · also of Dawn (ἐυπλόκαμος Ἠώς ’fine-plaited Dawn’)
ἐφάμην: φημί — say, speak; impf. mid. 1 sg., epic uncontracted: ’I was speaking, I spoke’
ἑζόμενοι: ἕζομαι — sit down; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’seated’
ἑξείης: ἑξείης — in order, one after another; adv. (Attic ἑξῆς)
ἑξῆς: ἑξῆς — in order, one after another; adv. (by-form of ἑξείης)
ἑπτὰ: ἑπτά — seven; numeral, indecl. (ἑπτὰ καὶ δέκα ’seventeen’)
ἑτάροις: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); masc. dat. pl. (= Attic ἑταίροις)
ἑτάροισι: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); dat. pl., epic -οισι
ἑτάροισιν: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἑτάρους: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); acc. pl.
ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.
ἑταῖρον: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. sg.
ἔδησαν: δέω — bind, make fast; aor. 3 pl.
ἔμ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (ἔμ’ = ἐμέ): ’me’
ἔμπεδον: ἔμπεδος — steady, firm, unbroken; adj., neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’steadily, without a break’
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔπειγε: ἐπείγω — press, urge on, hasten; impf. 3 sg.: ’was pressing’
ἔπειτ: ἔπειτα (elided ἔπειτ’) — then, next, after that
ἔπλετο: πέλομαι — be, become, happen; aor. 3 sg. used with pres. force: ’is’ · also with ordinary past/aorist force: ’came to be, arose’ (τοῦτο νόημα ἔπλετο ’this thought has arisen’)
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔστ: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., elided (ἔστ’ = ἔστι)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἔτ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided (ἔτ’ = ἔτι)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἕκαστα: ἕκαστος — each, every; neut. acc. pl. used substantivally: ’each thing, everything’
ἕλικας: ἕλιξ — twisted, curved (of cattle’s horns); fem. acc. pl.
ἕνα: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; masc. acc. sg. (ἕνα θυμόν ’one mind’)
ἕταροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl., epic by-form ἕταροι (= ἑταῖροι)
ἕτερον: ἕτερος — the other (of two); masc./neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., ’one (part)’, correlative: ἕτερον μὲν θειλόπεδον ... ἑτέρας δέ ’one part a drying-ground ... other parts’
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠελίου: ἥλιος (epic ἠέλιος) — sun; masc. gen. sg.
ἠελίῳ: ἥλιος — sun; masc. dat. sg., epic ἠέλιος (= Attic ἥλιος)
ἠνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἠνώγει, beside unaugmented ἀνώγει elsewhere in this part), + inf.: ’was bidding’
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’ · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a pool of water (ἡ δὲ προσέπλαζε ’and it lapped up’)
ἡμέων: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; gen. pl. ’of us’, epic uncontracted (= Attic ἡμῶν)
ἡμῖν: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; dat. pl. ’to us’
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’
ἢν: ἐάν (ἤν) — if (= εἰ + ἄν); conj. + subj.; ἢν μή ’unless’
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’ · also ’than’ after a comparative: μεῖζον … ἤ ’greater than’
ἤλυθεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; epic aor. 3 sg. (= Attic ἦλθεν): ’came’
ἤματι: ἦμαρ — day; neut. dat. sg., epic ἤματι
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἰαίνετο: ἰαίνω — warm, heat; impf. pass. 3 sg.: ’was being warmed’
ἰθάκην: Ἰθάκη — Ithaca, Odysseus’ island home; acc. sg.
ἰότητι: ἰότης — will, wish, favour; fem. dat. sg.: ’by the will of’
ἰών: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἱστοπέδῃ: ἱστοπέδη — mast-step, the block in which the mast stands; fem. dat. sg.
ἲς: ἴς (gen. ἰνός) — force, strength, might; fem. nom. sg., in the periphrasis ἱερὴ ἲς + gen. ’the sacred strength of ...’, i.e. the hero himself · also plain ’force, might’ of a thing: ἲς ἀνέμοιο ’the force of the wind’
ἴδμεν: οἶδα — know; pres. 1 pl., epic ἴδμεν (= Attic ἴσμεν): ’we know’
ἴδμεναι: οἶδα — know; perf. inf., epic ἴδμεναι (= Attic εἰδέναι)
ἴθυνε: ἰθύνω — make straight, steer; impf. (or aor.) 3 sg.: ’kept on a straight course’
ἴκμενον: ἴκμενος — favorable, following (of a wind); masc. acc. sg., in the formula ἴκμενον οὖρον
ἴφια: ἴφιος — stout, sturdy (the traditional gloss; ’fat’ also given); neut. acc. pl., with μῆλα
ἵει: ἵημι — send, let go, throw; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented
ἵκοισθε: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive; aor. opt. 2 pl., potential with κε: ’you may reach’ (Attic ἀφίκοισθε)
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’
ὀδυσεῦ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., single-σ form (Attic Ὀδυσσεῦ)
ὀλέσας: ὄλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having lost’
ὀξέι: ὀξύς — sharp; masc./neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ὀξεῖ)
ὀρθὸν: ὀρθός — upright, straight; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with the pronoun σ’
ὁμοῦ: ὁμοῦ — together, together with, at the same place; adv.
ὄλεθρον: ὄλεθρος — destruction, ruin, death; acc. sg.
ὄπ: ὄψ — voice; fem. acc. sg., elided (ὄπ’ = ὄπα)
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj. · also temporal ’until’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἵκετ’ Ἀρήτην ’until he came to Arete’) · also ’until’ + ἄν and subj. (ὄφρ’ ἂν ἵκηαι ’until you reach’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary verb: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρ’ … μένοιεν)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅπλα: ὅπλον — tool, gear; pl. ship’s tackle and rigging (not weapons here); neut. acc. pl.
ὅσ: ὅσος — as much/many as; relative correlative pron., neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσ’ = ὅσα)
ὅσον: ὅσος — as much as, as many as; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; neut. often adverbial: ’as much as’
ὅσσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος (double σ), neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’as many as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’)
ὑμέας: σύ (pl. ὑμεῖς) — you; acc. pl., epic ὑμέας (= Attic ὑμᾶς)
ὑπὲκ: ὑπέκ — out from under, forth from beneath; prep. + acc.; here in tmesis with φύγοιμεν: ’flee out from under’ (ὑπὲκ κακότητα φύγοιμεν)
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’) · also + dat., marking the agent with a passive verb: ’by’ (ὑπὸ μνηστῆρσιν δαμείη ’be overcome by the suitors’) · also + gen., ’from under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο) · also + gen., marking agent with a passive verb/participle beyond dying, ’by’: μεγάλου ὑπὸ κύματος ἀρθείς ’lifted up by a great wave’ · also + gen., of cause: ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς ’at the rush (of the throw)’
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
ὕστερον: ὕστερος — later, latter; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’afterwards’
ὠκύαλος: Ὠκύαλος — Ocyalus (’Swift-sea’), a Phaeacian youth; masc. nom. sg.
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὤτρυνον: ὀτρύνω — urge on, spur, exhort; impf. 3 pl., augmented: ’they urged on’ · also impf. 1 sg.: ’I urged on’
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
